json_result.metric: max abs error over exhaustive legal FP16 domain (> -1), vs FP64 log1p

evidence.summary: Exhaustive sweep of all 47,104 legal FP16 values (> -1, finite) through the kernel on CUDA vs FP64 log1p: 55 values violate the 1e-6 absolute tolerance; max abs error 1.3007e-6 at x=3378 (kernel 8.125333786, reference 8.125335087). Errors cluster in the large-x region (x in thousands), consistent with truncated polynomial coefficients (0.142857/0.2/0.33333) and split ln2 constants. These inputs are explicitly legal per the contract.

rationale: The atanh-series polynomial truncates after z^5/5 terms; residual term is ~z^7/7 with z up to ~0.245 (mantissa up to 1.65 after halving), giving truncation error possibly above 1e-6, and the ln2 constants (0.69313812256 + 9.058e-6) may not sum to ln2 exactly enough for large exponents. Exhaustive FP16 sweep can decide.

scope_evidence.summary: Every finite FP16 value strictly greater than -1 is legal ... Every output element must satisfy: abs(actual[i] - log(1 + x[i])) <= 1e-6. Correctness is one verdict for the implementation ... throughout the entire legal domain.

scope_rationale: Contract requires abs error <= 1e-6 for every finite FP16 value > -1; any legal input exceeding tolerance is a contract violation.
statement: There exist legal FP16 input values > -1 for which the kernel's output deviates from log(1+x) by more than 1e-6 absolute.
